title: Rectangle in a semicircle

answer:
Place the semicircle as the upper half of  
\[
x^2+y^2=25,\qquad y\ge 0.
\]
Let the upper-right vertex of the inscribed rectangle be \((x,y)\) on the arc, so
\[
x^2+y^2=25.
\]
By symmetry, the rectangle has width \(2x\) and height \(y\). Thus its area is
\[
A=2xy=2x\sqrt{25-x^2},\qquad 0<x<5.
\]

Differentiate:
\[
A(x)=2x(25-x^2)^{1/2},
\]
\[
A'(x)=2(25-x^2)^{1/2}+2x\cdot \frac{-x}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}
= \frac{2(25-2x^2)}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}.
\]
Set \(A'(x)=0\):
\[
25-2x^2=0 \implies x^2=\frac{25}{2}.
\]
So
\[
x=\frac{5}{\sqrt2},\qquad y=\sqrt{25-x^2}
=\sqrt{25-\frac{25}{2}}=\frac{5}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
A_{\max}=2xy
=2\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt2}\right)\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt2}\right)
=25.
\]

Check another way: let
\[
x=5\cos\theta,\qquad y=5\sin\theta.
\]
Then
\[
A=2xy=2(5\cos\theta)(5\sin\theta)
=50\sin\theta\cos\theta
=25\sin 2\theta.
\]
Since \(\sin 2\theta\le 1\), we get
\[
A\le 25,
\]
with equality when \(2\theta=90^\circ\), i.e. \(\theta=45^\circ\), so \(x=y=\frac{5}{\sqrt2}\).

\[
\boxed{25}
\]

The maximum area of the rectangle is \(\boxed{25}\) square units.
